subject: humanities
passage: To identify the author of an anonymous play, scholars sometimes compare how often it uses common function words such as "the," "and," and "of," on the theory that writers use these words out of unconscious habit. Function-word rates, however, also differ by genre: comedies, with their quick exchanges of dialogue, tend to use them differently from tragedies, whatever the author. One study compared an anonymous comedy from the 1590s with the known plays of two candidate authors. The first candidate wrote mainly comedies; all of the surviving plays by the second are tragedies. The anonymous play's function-word rates closely matched those of the first candidate. Because of how the comparison was set up, this match ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: establishes that the first candidate must be the author of the anonymous play.
choices.B: may reflect a shared genre as much as a shared author.
choices.C: proves that writers choose function words deliberately to suit each genre.
choices.D: shows that the anonymous play is more likely a tragedy than a comedy.

explanation.why: Function-word rates depend partly on genre. The anonymous play is a comedy, the first candidate's plays are mostly comedies, and the second's are all tragedies. A close match with the first candidate is therefore expected from genre alone, whoever wrote the play, so the study cannot separate genre from authorship.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Because genre could explain the match, it cannot establish authorship.
explanation.B: Correct. The comparison pits comedies against tragedies, so the match could come from genre rather than from the author.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text describes function-word use as unconscious habit and says nothing about deliberate choice.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text identifies the anonymous play as a comedy.
